notes: Full factorial pollination x herbivory; inflorescence density has opposing diffuse agent-mediated selection; joint covariance reconstructed and frozen in BALANCE_FRAGARIA_Q1B_RECEIPT_V1.
Pollinators favor later flowering and herbivores earlier flowering; no trait x pollination x herbivory interaction was significant so the conflict is additive rather than diffuse.
HCN x pollination x herbivory factorial; pollinators did not independently affect selection on a registered same trait while herbivory effects occurred on other or HCN-modified traits.
Damage changed direct selection but pollinator-mediated delta-beta was near zero and pollination x damage x trait contrasts were unsupported.
Pollinators favor long scapes and grazers short scapes but the estimand is a genetically based long-vs-short morph relative-fitness contrast rather than continuous standardized beta.
Multiseason field study plus separate pollen supplementation and artificial herbivory experiments suggest opposing forces on floral redness but do not form one crossed Q1B experiment.

Fragrance pollination and florivore manipulations identify a fitness cost of enhanced fragrance through florivores but the focal trait is experimentally set rather than a phenotypic-selection coordinate.

Ambush bugs reverse pollinator-mediated selection on daily display size through pollinator behavior; predator is an indirect context modifier rather than a second plant-fitness selection route on the trait.

Aphids were removed before pollination and chiefly changed phenotype; authors interpret herbivory as plasticity context modifying bumblebee-mediated selection rather than direct opposing agent-mediated selection.

Full 2x2 bee/hand pollination x caterpillar herbivory over six generations demonstrates interactive evolutionary response but does not supply the registered within-study Q1B selection contrast vector.
Open vs pollen-supplemented plants identify pollinator-mediated selection; antagonist damage was observational and did not alter selection on floral traits.
Herbivore exclusion changes the floral selection regime and ungulates prefer larger plants but pollination is not experimentally toggled to identify pollinator-mediated beta.
Pollination is experimentally manipulated but slugs weevils and caterpillars enter through path analysis rather than a crossed antagonist intervention.

Manipulated pollination florivory and nectar robbing have nonadditive effects on later visitors traits and reproduction but the analysis is treatment-response rather than agent-mediated phenotypic selection on one continuous trait.
Pieris brassicae acts in the system as both pollinating visitor and herbivore/host-use agent so it cannot provide a clean independent antagonist axis against pollination.
